reason: I want to build the pump, and heart muscle fits the chambers' pumping walls slot.
expectation: I expect the heart muscle to form pumping walls around the chambers, though the pump will still need valves and a rhythm.

alternatives.reason: Valves also fit a named chamber slot, but I chose to add the pumping walls first.

effect: The chambers now have muscular walls, so I can add direction control next.
reaction: The thickening walls make the pump's action clear.
reason: Valves fit the remaining chamber slot and should direct blood flow.
expectation: I expect the valves to be fitted into the chambers and help prevent reverse flow.

effect: The valves provide direction control, and the pacemaker cells can now be added to the chambers.
reaction: The forward and reverse arrows clearly show what the valves do.
reason: Adding pacemaker cells should give the pump its rhythm and advance the first goal.
expectation: I expect the cells to help coordinate rhythmic contractions, completing the pump or bringing it closer to completion.

effect: The pacemaker completed the beating heart, leaving the exchange route to build.
reaction: The heart starting its own beat was interesting; I had expected coordinated contractions.
reason: Joining the vessels and capillaries should create the exchange route and a path back to the heart.
expectation: I expect a connected vessel network with capillaries between arteries and veins, though it may still need to be connected to the heart.

alternatives.reason: Oxygen-carrying cells also seem necessary, but I want to build their route first.

effect: The capillaries now connect the outward and returning vessels; the remaining offered action builds oxygen-carrying cells.
reaction: The arrows make the return route clear, though the circuit still appears to need the heart.
reason: This is the only available combination, and hemoglobin should give the red cells a way to carry oxygen.
expectation: I expect red blood cells containing hemoglobin, ready to carry oxygen through the circuit.

effect: The red cells contain hemoglobin and make ATP from sugar without mitochondria; the next offered step combines them with plasma.
reaction: The absence of mitochondria was interesting, though the brief description leaves me wondering why.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and plasma should provide the fluid carrying the red cells.
expectation: I expect blood containing red cells suspended in plasma, ready to enter the vessel circuit.

effect: The blood now contains red cells in plasma, with sugar dissolved in the surrounding fluid. It can be added to the vessel circuit.
reaction: The picture makes the different contents of the cells and plasma clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and putting blood into the vessels should advance the exchange route.
expectation: I expect the blood to fill the connected vessels; the circuit may still need to be connected to the heart.

effect: The blood-filled vessels can exchange oxygen and nutrients with tissue and carry carbon dioxide away when supplied. The next goal is to put the blood into circulation.
reaction: The inset makes the exchange clear, including that red cells stay inside the capillary.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and connecting the heart to the blood-filled circuit should put blood into circulation.
expectation: I expect the beating heart to pump blood through the circuit and back to itself.

effect: The heart and blood-filled vessels now form a closed circulation, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate pump and vessel route come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Putting blood into the vessel circuit was most worthwhile because the tissue exchange inset connected circulation to the cells' need for oxygen and nutrients.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining red cells with plasma was straightforward but less engaging; it mainly assembled components whose roles were already apparent.

surprise.text: I was interested that red blood cells make ATP from sugar despite having no mitochondria. I was left wondering why they lack them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though several later combinations were the only available choice, so they felt more like following an assembly sequence than making a decision.

continue.text: I would continue to see how circulation connects with other body systems. The exchange and closed-loop descriptions made those connections interesting, although I would hope for more meaningful choices.
